[[Category:BITwiki Schema Matter]]
<includeonly>

= BITwiki Template Usage Guide: Best Practices for Template Implementation =

== Etymology: The Craft of Pattern ==

''Usage'' — from Latin ''usus'', from ''uti'', to use, to employ. The act of employing, the practice of application. Usage is not mere consumption but skilled employment—the craft of putting patterns to work.

''Guide'' — from Old French ''guider'', to guide, lead, conduct. From a Germanic root meaning to have charge of, to watch over. A guide is not a commander but a companion—one who has traveled the path and marks the way.

== Purpose: Guidance Without Constraint ==

This document provides guidelines for using templates in BITwiki. Templates ensure consistent formatting, enable semantic markup, and facilitate knowledge reuse.

This guide offers:
* '''Orientation''': Finding the right template for your content
* '''Instruction''': Understanding how to use template parameters
* '''Troubleshooting''': Resolving common issues
* '''Best practices''': Patterns that have proven effective
* '''Confidence systems''': Understanding multiple representation approaches

It does not command. It accompanies.

== Template Selection: Finding the Right Pattern ==

=== Step 1: Identify Entity Type ===

Determine the type of content:
* Concept: Use Template:Infobox Concept
* Idea: Use Template:Infobox Idea
* Implementation: Use Template:Infobox Implementation
* Project: Use Template:Infobox Project

=== Step 2: Check for Specialized Templates ===

Some domains have specialized templates:
* Person: Template:Infobox Person
* Organization: Template:Infobox Organization
* Publication: Template:Infobox Publication
* Event: Template:Infobox Event

=== Step 3: Consider Navigation Templates ===

For page organization:
* Navigation boxes: Template:Navbox
* Sidebars: Template:Sidebar
* Portals: Template:Portal

== Parameter Usage: Filling the Pattern ==

=== Required Parameters ===

Always provide required parameters:
* name: Entity name
* definition/description: Brief description
* epistemic_status: One of the established tiers
* confidence: Qualitative level (low, medium, high, very high, well-established)

Example:
```wiki
{{Infobox Idea
| name = Feedback Loop
| definition = A process where outputs are fed back as inputs
| epistemic_status = Verified
| confidence = high
}}
```

=== Optional Parameters ===

Add optional parameters when relevant:
* image: Illustrative image
* originator: Who originated the idea
* date: When originated
* sources: Number of sources

Example:
```wiki
{{Infobox Idea
| name = Feedback Loop
| definition = A process where outputs are fed back as inputs
| originator = Norbert Wiener
| date = 1948
| epistemic_status = Verified
| confidence = high
| sources = 1000
}}
```

=== Parameter Formatting ===

Text: Plain text, no markup
```wiki
| name = Feedback Loop
```

Dates: ISO 8601 format
```wiki
| date = 1948
```

Pages: Wiki page names
```wiki
| originator = Person:Norbert Wiener
```

Lists: Comma-separated
```wiki
| related = Homeostasis, Control Theory
```

== Confidence Representation Systems ==

BITwiki supports multiple confidence representation approaches. Choose the system appropriate for your context:

=== Textual Confidence Levels ===

For qualitative assessment using descriptive terms:

| Level | Meaning | Use Case |
|-------|---------|----------|
| low | Preliminary, speculative | Early hypotheses, unverified claims |
| medium | Moderate support | Some evidence exists but limited |
| high | Strong support | Substantial evidence, consensus |
| very high | Near certainty | Extensive validation, established fact |
| well-established | Canonical acceptance | Definitive, widely recognized |

Example:
```wiki
| confidence = high
```

=== Numeric Confidence Scores ===

For quantitative assessment using decimal values:

| Score Range | Interpretation | Corresponding Textual |
|-------------|----------------|----------------------|
| 0.00-0.25 | low | low |
| 0.26-0.50 | medium | medium |
| 0.51-0.75 | high | high |
| 0.76-0.90 | very high | very high |
| 0.91-1.00 | well-established | well-established |

Example:
```wiki
| confidence_score = 0.95
```

=== Confidence Trajectory ===

For tracking confidence evolution over time:

The confidence trajectory represents how confidence in a claim changes as evidence accumulates. Document the trajectory using:

```wiki
[[Has confidence trajectory::{{{confidence|established}}}]]
```

Trajectory values: emerging → developing → established → canonical

== Best Practices: Patterns for Excellence ==

=== Practice 1: Complete All Required Parameters ===

Poor:
```wiki
{{Infobox Idea
| name = Feedback Loop
}}
```

Better:
```wiki
{{Infobox Idea
| name = Feedback Loop
| definition = A process where outputs are fed back as inputs
| epistemic_status = Verified
| confidence = high
}}
```

=== Practice 2: Use Consistent Formatting ===

Poor:
```wiki
| name=Feedback Loop
| definition = A process
```

Better:
```wiki
| name = Feedback Loop
| definition = A process where outputs are fed back as inputs
```

=== Practice 3: Provide Accurate Information ===

Poor:
```wiki
| confidence = very high
| sources = 10000
```

Better:
```wiki
| confidence = high
| sources = 5
```

Or using numeric:
```wiki
| confidence_score = 0.85
| sources = 5
```

=== Practice 4: Update When Information Changes ===

Poor:
* Never updating outdated information

Better:
* Regular review and updates
* Version tracking
* Change documentation
* Confidence trajectory updates

== Troubleshooting: Resolving Issues ==

=== Issue 1: Template Not Displaying ===

Symptoms: Template code visible, not rendered

Causes:
* Template doesn't exist
* Syntax error
* Missing closing brackets

Solutions:
* Check template name
* Verify syntax
* Check for typos
* Ensure template page exists

=== Issue 2: Parameters Not Working ===

Symptoms: Default values shown instead of custom values

Causes:
* Parameter name misspelled
* Parameter not supported
* Case sensitivity
* Confidence value format mismatch

Solutions:
* Check parameter name
* Verify template documentation
* Check case
* Ensure confidence value matches expected format (textual vs numeric)

=== Issue 3: SMW Properties Not Generated ===

Symptoms: No semantic properties in page

Causes:
* Template missing SMW markup
* <includeonly> tags missing
* Property syntax error
* Confidence property name mismatch

Solutions:
* Check template SMW markup
* Verify <includeonly> tags
* Check property syntax
* Verify property name matches (confidence vs confidence_score vs confidence trajectory)

=== Issue 4: Validation Errors ===

Symptoms: Page in error category

Causes:
* Invalid confidence value
* Missing required parameter
* Invalid epistemic status
* Confidence score out of range (0.0-1.0)

Solutions:
* Check confidence value against valid options
* Add missing parameters
* Use valid epistemic status
* Verify numeric confidence is within 0.0-1.0 range

=== Issue 5: Confidence System Conflicts ===

Symptoms: Multiple confidence values showing, inconsistent display

Causes:
* Mixing textual and numeric confidence in same template
* Template expecting one format, receiving another
* Legacy templates using deprecated confidence format

Solutions:
* Use consistent confidence format per template
* Check template documentation for expected format
* Update legacy templates to current standard
* Use confidence mapping for conversions

== Advanced Usage: Extending Patterns ==

=== Nested Templates ===

Templates can include other templates:
```wiki
{{Infobox Idea
| name = Feedback Loop
| definition = {{Definition:Feedback}}
| epistemic_status = Verified
}}
```

=== Conditional Parameters ===

Show content only if parameter exists:
```wiki
{{#if: {{{image|}}} | [[File:{{{image}}}]] | }}
```

=== Dynamic Properties ===

Generate properties dynamically:
```wiki
[[Has confidence::{{{confidence|medium}}}]]
[[Has confidence score::{{{confidence_score|0.5}}}]]
```

=== Confidence Conversion Templates ===

Convert between confidence representations:
```wiki
{{#switch: {{{confidence|}}}
| low = 0.15
| medium = 0.40
| high = 0.65
| very high = 0.85
| well-established = 0.95
| #default = 0.50
}}
```

== SMW Integration: Machine Readability ==

=== Template-Generated Properties ===

Templates automatically generate SMW properties:
```wiki
[[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has name::{{{name}}}]]
[[Has confidence::{{{confidence}}}]]
[[Has confidence score::{{{confidence_score}}}]]
[[Has confidence trajectory::{{{confidence_trajectory|established}}}]]
```

=== Querying Template Data ===

Query data from templates:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has confidence::high]]
}}
```

Query by numeric confidence:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has confidence score::>0.8]]
}}
```

Query by trajectory:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has confidence trajectory::established]]
}}
```

=== Combined Confidence Queries ===

Query across confidence systems:
```wiki
{{#ask: [[Has entity type::Idea]]
[[Has confidence::high||very high||well-established]]
[[Has confidence score::>0.7]]
}}
```

== Version History ==

This consolidated document merges content from multiple source versions:
* '''v2.0.0''' (2026-02-12): Original numeric confidence system (confidence_score: 0.0-1.0)
* '''v2.1.0-revised''' (2026-02-14): Added etymology section, textual confidence system (low/medium/high/very high)
* '''v2.established''' (2026-02-12): Introduced confidence trajectory concept
* '''v3.0.0-consolidated''' (2026-02-17): Merged all systems, added mapping tables, enhanced documentation

# BITwiki Ontology Index. (2026).
# BITwiki Constitution. (2026).

| 0.91-1.00 | well-established | well-established |

```wiki
| confidence_score = 0.95
```

=== Confidence Trajectory ===

For tracking confidence evolution over time:

The confidence trajectory represents how confidence in a claim changes as evidence accumulates. Document the trajectory using:

```wiki
[[Has confidence trajectory::{{{confidence|established}}}]]
```

```wiki

| name = Feedback Loop
}}
```

Better:
```wiki

}}
```


Better:

```wiki

| sources = 10000
```

Better:
```wiki

| sources = 5
```

```wiki

```

=== Practice 4: Update When Information Changes ===

Poor:
* Never updating outdated information

Better:
* Regular review and updates
* Version tracking
* Change documentation
* Confidence trajectory updates

== Troubleshooting: Resolving Issues ==

=== Issue 1: Template Not Displaying ===

Symptoms: Template code visible, not rendered

Causes:
* Template doesn't exist
* Syntax error
* Missing closing brackets

Solutions:
* Check template name
* Verify syntax
* Check for typos
* Ensure template page exists

=== Issue 2: Parameters Not Working ===

Symptoms: Default values shown instead of custom values

Causes:
* Parameter name misspelled
* Parameter not supported
* Case sensitivity
* Confidence value format mismatch

Solutions:
* Check parameter name
* Verify template documentation
* Check case
* Ensure confidence value matches expected format (textual vs numeric)

=== Issue 3: SMW Properties Not Generated ===

Symptoms: No semantic properties in page

Causes:
* Template missing SMW markup
* <includeonly> tags missing
* Property syntax error
* Confidence property name mismatch

Solutions:
* Check template SMW markup
* Verify <includeonly> tags
* Check property syntax
* Verify property name matches (confidence vs confidence_score vs confidence trajectory)

=== Issue 4: Validation Errors ===

Symptoms: Page in error category

Causes:
* Invalid confidence value
* Missing required parameter
* Invalid epistemic status
* Confidence score out of range (0.0-1.0)

Solutions:
* Check confidence value against valid options
* Add missing parameters
* Use valid epistemic status
* Verify numeric confidence is within 0.0-1.0 range

=== Issue 5: Confidence System Conflicts ===

Symptoms: Multiple confidence values showing, inconsistent display

Causes:
* Mixing textual and numeric confidence in same template
* Template expecting one format, receiving another
* Legacy templates using deprecated confidence format

Solutions:
* Use consistent confidence format per template
* Check template documentation for expected format
* Update legacy templates to current standard
* Use confidence mapping for conversions

== Advanced Usage: Extending Patterns ==

=== Nested Templates ===

Templates can include other templates:
```wiki

| name = Feedback Loop
| definition = {{Definition:Feedback}}
| epistemic_status = Verified
}}
```

=== Conditional Parameters ===

Show content only if parameter exists:
```wiki
{{#if: {{{image|}}} | [[File:{{{image}}}]] | }}
```

=== Dynamic Properties ===

Generate properties dynamically:
```wiki
[[Has confidence::{{{confidence|medium}}}]]
[[Has confidence score::{{{confidence_score|0.5}}}]]
```

=== Confidence Conversion Templates ===

Convert between confidence representations:
```wiki

| low = 0.15
| medium = 0.40
| high = 0.65
| very high = 0.85
| well-established = 0.95
| #default = 0.50
}}
```

Templates automatically generate SMW properties:


```wiki
}}
```

```wiki

}}
```

Query by trajectory:
```wiki

}}
```

```wiki

```

= BITwiki Template Usage Guide: Best Practices for Template Implementation =

== Etymology: The Craft of Pattern ==

''Usage'' — from Latin ''usus'', from ''uti'', to use, to employ. The act of employing, the practice of application. Usage is not mere consumption but skilled employment—the craft of putting patterns to work.

''Guide'' — from Old French ''guider'', to guide, lead, conduct. From a Germanic root meaning to have charge of, to watch over. A guide is not a commander but a companion—one who has traveled the path and marks the way.

== Purpose: Guidance Without Constraint ==

This document provides guidelines for using templates in BITwiki. Templates ensure consistent formatting, enable semantic markup, and facilitate knowledge reuse.

This guide offers:
* '''Orientation''': Finding the right template for your content
* '''Instruction''': Understanding how to use template parameters
* '''Troubleshooting''': Resolving common issues
* '''Best practices''': Patterns that have proven effective
* '''Confidence systems''': Understanding multiple representation approaches

It does not command. It accompanies.

== Template Selection: Finding the Right Pattern ==

=== Step 1: Identify Entity Type ===

Determine the type of content:
* Concept: Use Template:Infobox Concept
* Idea: Use Template:Infobox Idea
* Implementation: Use Template:Infobox Implementation
* Project: Use Template:Infobox Project

=== Step 2: Check for Specialized Templates ===

Some domains have specialized templates:
* Person: Template:Infobox Person
* Organization: Template:Infobox Organization
* Publication: Template:Infobox Publication
* Event: Template:Infobox Event

=== Step 3: Consider Navigation Templates ===

* Navigation boxes: Template:Navbox
* Sidebars: Template:Sidebar
* Portals: Template:Portal

== Parameter Usage: Filling the Pattern ==

=== Required Parameters ===

Always provide required parameters:
* name: Entity name
* definition/description: Brief description
* epistemic_status: One of the established tiers
* confidence: Qualitative level (low, medium, high, very high, well-established)

Example:
```wiki
{{Infobox Idea
| name = Feedback Loop
| definition = A process where outputs are fed back as inputs
| epistemic_status = Verified
| confidence = high
}}
```

=== Optional Parameters ===

Add optional parameters when relevant:
* image: Illustrative image
* originator: Who originated the idea
* date: When originated
* sources: Number of sources

Example:
```wiki

| definition = A process where outputs are fed back as inputs
| originator = Norbert Wiener
| date = 1948
| epistemic_status = Verified
| confidence = high
| sources = 1000
}}
```

Text: Plain text, no markup
```wiki

```

Dates: ISO 8601 format
```wiki

```

Pages: Wiki page names
```wiki
| originator = Person:Norbert Wiener
```

Lists: Comma-separated
```wiki

```

BITwiki supports multiple confidence representation approaches. Choose the system appropriate for your context:

For qualitative assessment using descriptive terms:

| Level | Meaning | Use Case |
|-------|---------|----------|
| low | Preliminary, speculative | Early hypotheses, unverified claims |
| medium | Moderate support | Some evidence exists but limited |
| high | Strong support | Substantial evidence, consensus |
| very high | Near certainty | Extensive validation, established fact |
| well-established | Canonical acceptance | Definitive, widely recognized |

Example:
```wiki
| confidence = high
```

| 0.26-0.50 | medium | medium |
| 0.51-0.75 | high | high |
